Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the failing test does:
  - DetectCompressorTestCase.testDetection() tries to auto-detect and open several compressed files via a helper getStreamFor(...). One of them is "bla.tar.deflatez", which (per the issue description) is a deflate stream wrapped with a zlib header.

- How auto-detection works in the code:
  - CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream(InputStream) reads the first bytes of the stream and tests them against known signatures in a fixed order:
    - BZip2CompressorInputStream.matches(...)
    - GzipCompressorInputStream.matches(...)
    - Pack200CompressorInputStream.matches(...)
    - FramedSnappyCompressorInputStream.matches(...)
    - ZCompressorInputStream.matches(...)  [this is Unix “compress” (.Z), not zlib/deflate]
    - XZ (via XZUtils.matches(...))
    - LZMA (via LZMAUtils.matches(...))
  - If none match, it throws CompressorException("No Compressor found for the stream signature.").

- Why "bla.tar.deflatez" isn’t detected:
  - There is no signature check for deflate-with-zlib-header in CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream(InputStream). The only “Z” check present is for the legacy .Z format, not zlib/deflate.
  - As a result, a stream starting with a zlib header (e.g., 0x78 0x9C, 0x78 0xDA, etc.) doesn’t match any of the tested signatures and the factory throws the “No Compressor found...” exception, which causes testDetection() to fail when it reaches the deflatez file.

- Evidence of available but unused support:
  - There is a DeflateCompressorInputStream that can handle both raw deflate and deflate with zlib headers depending on DeflateParameters.withZlibHeader(). Its constructor ultimately creates a java.util.zip.Inflater with nowrap set according to withZlibHeader().
  - However, createCompressorInputStream(InputStream) never attempts to detect or instantiate DeflateCompressorInputStream; only the name-based overload createCompressorInputStream(String, InputStream) handles DEFLATE (and even there, it uses the default parameters, which may or may not default to expecting a zlib header).

- Conclusion:
  - The failure is due to missing auto-detection for deflate streams with a zlib header in CompressorStreamFactory.createCompressorInputStream(InputStream). The code currently confuses none of the formats with zlib/deflate and thus never selects DeflateCompressorInputStream for “.deflatez” inputs, leading to the thrown CompressorException and the test failure.
